speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN).

The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant presenting with respiratory distress within two hours of birth, following an uneventful pregnancy, is classic for TTN due to delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid. No further testing is required to confirm this clinical diagnosis.
